entries.tutorialSubtitle: The classic marzipan-wrapped chequerboard sponge in pink and yellow
entries.tutorialExcerpt: A battenberg is two almond sponges baked together, cut into strips, glued with apricot jam into a two-by-two chequerboard, and wrapped tightly in marzipan. The method is logical and the result is impressive; the work lies in cutting the sponge strips to a consistent size so the pattern reads clearly at every slice.

entries.tutorialSubtitle: How to make chocolate curls, shavings, cigarellos, and bark splinters for cake decoration
entries.tutorialExcerpt: Chocolate curls are made by drawing a peeler or a large knife across a block of chocolate at the right temperature: cold chocolate shards, warm chocolate smears, and chocolate at about 18 to 20 degrees Celsius curls cleanly. entries.tutorialSubtitle: Spanish melt-in-the-mouth almond and lard shortbread
entries.tutorialExcerpt: Polvorones are a Spanish Christmas shortbread made with toasted flour, ground almonds, lard, and cinnamon. You get a very fragile biscuit that crumbles the moment you bite into it. The toasted flour is not optional: it is what gives polvorones their particular nutty, dry flavour.

entries.tutorialSubtitle: piped butter biscuits sandwiched with jam and buttercream
entries.tutorialExcerpt: Viennese whirls are piped butter biscuits with a very high fat content that gives them a melt-in-the-mouth texture. You get a sandwiched biscuit with a layer of buttercream and raspberry jam in the centre. The dough must be soft enough to pipe through a star nozzle but firm enough that the rosette holds its shape in the oven.
